text.p: - Slovenia and China should strengthen their economic ties, President Milan Kucan said during a six-day visit to China.

- Representatives of the successor states of the former Yugoslavia, who met in Brussels this week, failed agree on the division of assets of the former federation. Their next meeting is due to take place in Brussels on November 11 and 12.
- Defence Minister Jelko Kacin started a two-day visit to the Czech Republic on Tuesday.
- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek and his Hungarian counterpart Gyula Horn, meeting in Budapest on Tuesday, said there were no major problems between their two countries.
- A member of the State Council (the upper house of parliament) was robbed and beaten in front of his appartment in Ljubljana on Monday night.
- August monthly gross salaries in Slovenia were down 0.4 percent from July.
- Slovenia's biggest trade union ZSSS said it would stage a two-hour strike on October 24 in employers refuse to retract plans to cut work benefits.
- Parliament passed a law on the use of agricultural land, replacing an old law that will expire this month.

- British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind said Slovenia was a strong candidate for full membership in the European Union and NATO. He met his Slovenian counterpart Davorin Kracun in London on Tuesday.
- Bank SKB is expected to decide whether to grant foreign investors a bigger equity stake in the bank. Currently, foreigners hold about 30 percent of the shares.
